'''Narawake''' (''narawake'') was a figure of ancient {{ill|Japan|ja|日本}}. Also written as '''Narawake-no-Ōkimi'''.

He was the ancestor of the {{ill|Shimotsukenu clan|ja|下毛野氏|lt=Shimotsukeno-no-Kimi}}, said to be a descendant of {{ill|Toyoki-Iribiko-no-Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命}}, a prince of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}}.

== Records ==
No deeds are recorded in the ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}}''. The sources cited below also differ as to whether he was a fourth- or sixth-generation descendant.

In the {{ill|Shimotsukenu no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|下毛野国造}} entry of the "{{ill|Kokuzō Hongi|ja|国造本紀}}" of the ''{{ill|Sendai Kuji Hongi|ja|先代旧事本紀}}'', it is recorded that during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}}, {{ill|Keno Province|ja|毛野国}} was divided into upper and lower, and Narawake — fourth-generation descendant of Toyoki-no-Mikoto — was appointed as the first {{ill|Shimotsukenu no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|下毛野国造}}.

In the ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|ja|新撰姓氏録}}'', the Ōami-no-Kimi entry records "the sixth-generation descendant of Toyoki-Iribiko-no-Mikoto: Shimotsuke-no-Kimi Nara"; the Kibikōbe entry has "sixth-generation descendant of Toyoki-Iribiko-no-Mikoto: Nara-no-Kimi" and notes his younger brother as "Mawaka-no-Kimi."

== Descendant clans ==
The ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|ja|新撰姓氏録}}'' records the following clan as descendants:
* Kōbetsu, Sakyō, Kibikōbe — same ancestor as the Kamitsukenu Asomi. Descendants of Nara-no-Kimi, sixth-generation descendant of Toyoki-Iribiko-no-Mikoto.

== Traditions ==
Shrines with traditions related to Narawake:
* {{ill|Utsunomiya Futaarayama Shrine|ja|宇都宮二荒山神社}} ({{ill|Utsunomiya|ja|宇都宮市|lt=Utsunomiya City}}, {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|ja|栃木県}}) — said to have been founded by Narawake-no-Ōkimi.
* {{ill|Nogi Shrine|ja|野木神社}} ({{ill|Nogi, Tochigi|ja|野木町|lt=Nogi Town}}, {{ill|Shimotsuga District|ja|下都賀郡}}, Tochigi Prefecture) — said to enshrine the remains of {{ill|Uji-no-Wakiiratsuko|ja|菟道稚郎子|lt=Uji-no-Wakiiratsuko-no-Mikoto|lt_ja=菟道稚郎子命}}, brought by Narawake-no-Ōkimi when he took up his post as Shimotsukenu no Kuni no Miyatsuko.
* Nara Shrine ({{ill|Kumagaya|ja|熊谷市|lt=Kumagaya City}}, {{ill|Saitama Prefecture|ja|埼玉県}}) — said to have been opened by Narawake-no-Mikoto after he finished his service as kuni no miyatsuko.
